mechanism_claims.claim_text: TroHepc2-22 directly perturbs bacterial membranes, with source evidence from DiSC3(5) membrane depolarization and PI permeability assays.
mechanism_claims.entity_scope: TroHepc2-22 against S. aureus, S. agalactiae, E. piscicida, and V. harveyi
mechanism_claims.limitations: Figure traces/images were used qualitatively; exact curve/image quantitation was not digitized.

mechanism_claims.claim_text: SEM evidence shows bacterial surface damage, membrane rupture, and cytoplasm leakage after TroHepc2-22 treatment.
mechanism_claims.entity_scope: TroHepc2-22 at 4x MIC against S. aureus, S. agalactiae, V. harveyi, and E. piscicida
mechanism_claims.limitations: Morphological claim is source-supported; no numeric damage fraction is available in local material.

mechanism_claims.claim_text: Gel-retardation evidence supports interaction with, and degradation of, bacterial genomic DNA after membrane penetration.
mechanism_claims.entity_scope: TroHepc2-22 against genomic DNA from S. aureus, S. agalactiae, E. piscicida, and V. harveyi
direct_assay_types: gel retardation assay with bacterial genomic DNA
mechanism_claims.limitations: Lane concentrations are preserved from figure caption; band intensity quantification is not locally tabulated.

mechanism_claims.claim_text: In vivo challenge data and immune-gene expression data support host protection and immune response association after TroHepc2-22 treatment before V. harveyi infection.
mechanism_claims.entity_scope: T. ovatus injected with TroHepc2-22 before V. harveyi challenge
mechanism_claims.limitations: This is not promoted to a direct antimicrobial molecular mechanism beyond the in vivo association and qRT-PCR readout.
